Hartford Public Schools
Family & Community Engagement Office
Family Event Food Allergen Labeling Guidance
Effective October 2026

Any dish served at a school family or community event must be posted with an
allergen card at the serving table. The card lists every major food allergen present
in that dish. The major allergens are: milk, eggs, wheat, soy, peanuts, tree nuts,
fish, and shellfish.

When a dish is prepared by an outside kitchen or vendor, the label the vendor
submits is a starting point, not the final word. The staff member coordinating the
event checks the submitted label against the food as actually prepared, using both
the tray photograph and the kitchen's written ingredient information, before any card
is posted or shared with families. An allergen is listed on the card if it appears in
any source. Some allergens are not visible in a photograph and are found only in the
kitchen's own description of the dish.

The card must reflect the food AS IT WILL BE SERVED. The most recent information
from the kitchen governs; an ingredient the kitchen has removed is no longer listed,
and an ingredient it has added must appear. A vendor's assurance that a dish is
'free' of an allergen does not replace this check.

If a submitted label is wrong or incomplete, hold the card. Do not post it and do not
send it to families until it has been corrected and approved by the building
administrator.

Questions: Family & Community Engagement Office, Hartford Public Schools.
